businessModel: None; free open-source hobby project from the Thorium author
channels: Release (SSE3, SSE4, AVX, AVX2, ARM64 builds)
updateCadence: None since Sep 2024; earlier releases came every 1-3 months
summary: A Firefox fork built with AVX/AVX2/LTO/PGO optimisations and privacy patches borrowed from LibreWolf, Waterfox and others. Its last release is Firefox 129 from September 2024, so it no longer gets security fixes.
bestFor: Readers curious about CPU-optimised Firefox builds
Users on old CPUs who want SSE3 or SSE4 builds (with the security caveat)
Anyone studying how Thorium's approach was applied to Gecko
notFor: Anyone browsing the open web today: it is more than 20 Firefox versions behind
People who need guaranteed security updates
Users who want a maintained fork, such as LibreWolf, Waterfox or Floorp

pros.title: CPU-targeted builds
pros.detail: Separate SSE3, SSE4, AVX, AVX2 and ARM64 builds with LTO and PGO; the developer claims 8-20% over stock Firefox (not independently verified).

pros.title: Firefox add-on ecosystem
pros.detail: Firefox base keeps the full add-on catalogue, MV2 and uBlock Origin.

pros.title: Portable packages
pros.detail: Windows and Linux zips run from a folder with a USER_DATA profile beside the launcher.

pros.title: Normandy disabled
pros.detail: The 129.0.2 notes say Mozilla's Normandy remote-config component is switched off.

cons.title: Abandoned in practice
cons.detail: No release since Sep 2024 and no maintainer reply on status issues; a collaborator says he will not publish further builds for now.

cons.title: Unpatched security flaws
cons.detail: Firefox 129 misses every security fix since 2024, and the maintainers said there was no timeline for security updates.

cons.title: Site compatibility drift
cons.detail: The engine is two years behind, so newer web features and anti-bot checks increasingly fail.

cons.title: Thin documentation
cons.detail: Patch list, telemetry defaults and default search are not summarised in the sources we could fetch.

signatureFeatures: Patches from LibreWolf, Waterfox, Ghostery and BetterFox

faq.a: Not officially, but there has been no release since 129.0.2 (17 Sep 2024) and no commit on main since 3 Dec 2024. Users on GitHub have repeatedly asked if it is abandoned.

faq.q: Is this the old Mercury iOS or Android browser?
faq.a: No. This is Alex313031's Firefox fork; the older Mercury Browser articles on Wikipedia are an unrelated Android browser.
Not for general browsing. It is built on Firefox 129 with no security updates since September 2024.

switching.note: Firefox-family profile; moving to LibreWolf, Waterfox or Floorp keeps extensions and most settings.

spec.codecs: Firefox 129 set; AV1 yes, HEVC partial (unverified)
spec.sandbox: Firefox sandbox and Fission, frozen at v129

jsSpeed: Firefox 129 with AVX/PGO/LTO; claimed gain unverified
pageLoad: Optimised Gecko, but an old engine
cpu: Instruction-set builds aim to cut CPU time
privacyDefaults: Patches from LibreWolf and BetterFox; list unverified
blocking: ETP only; uBlock Origin via add-ons
securityHardening: Sandbox intact but base is two years unpatched
patchSpeed: No release since Sep 2024; no update timeline
telemetry: Normandy off; rest of telemetry unverified
tabManagement: Pinned tabs and containers; add-ons for the rest
translation: Firefox translation features unconfirmed in builds
sync: Firefox Sync unverified in these builds
webCompat: Gecko 129 is far behind current Firefox
businessTrust: No business, but silent on project status
longevity: No releases for 13+ months; maintainers decline updates
beginnerFriendly: Five CPU variants per platform confuse newcomers
